question: When the creator reacts to material or events, how much of the reaction becomes a first-person confession or personal anecdote versus staying a verdict on the thing itself?
pole_low: verdict-only: judges the material, the self stays absent
pole_high: confession-led: most beats become a this-is-me story
why: MoreAliA's second sampled video runs almost entirely on identification - nearly every clip triggers a personal anecdote - while his first stays verdict-led. It decides whether Our Guy reacts as a judge or as a fellow sufferer, which is the whole warmth of a reaction-style avatar.
evidence_needed: Two or more videos per reaction-format creator; count beats that turn first-person versus beats that stay verdicts.

question: When the format provides no built-in staircase (no levels, no count, no growth bar), does the creator impose one anyway - ranking, counting, rematches - or ride the material's own flat shape?
pole_low: rides the format's shape as given
pole_high: imposes a staircase on shapeless material
why: Both creators in this lane split show-010 by format: ladders and house counts supplied escalation in one video, nothing did in the other. Whether escalation is a trait or a rental decides if Our Guy needs a self-built staircase habit for unstructured games.
evidence_needed: One format-free video per creator (no list, ladder or count in the premise); look for invented rankings, tallies or rematch structures.

question: How much does the creator's in-character depth follow the premise versus staying constant across formats?
pole_low: persona is fixed; every format bends to the same character depth
pole_high: persona is re-cast per premise; the host self underneath stays thin
why: UnspeakablePlays is fully in character when the premise casts him as a creature and a plain host when it does not. If persona depth is premise-slaved in the field, the avatar's character sheet needs a per-premise casting rule, not one immersion dial.
evidence_needed: Two contrasting formats per ensemble creator, shaded on show-005; measure the swing, not the average.

question: How seamlessly are asks (subscribe, sponsor, comments) performed as content at full in-show energy versus marked as interruptions where the frame and energy drop?
pole_low: asks are interruptions: energy drops, frame breaks, an admitted ad break
pole_high: asks are content: same voice, same energy, often a bit or a recurring gag
why: All four videos in this round do it the seamless way - an in-character sponsor read, a subscribe gag hidden inside a prank, a subscribe-animation pitch run as a recurring content bit. If seamless asks are a winners' trait, the avatar's own asks should be designed as beats, not breaks.
evidence_needed: Timestamped ask segments from at least three creators; compare energy and register in the thirty seconds before, during and after the ask.

question: After a surprise, how much does the creator reverse-engineer how it worked, aloud, versus consuming the surprise and moving on?
pole_high: surprise is reconstructed in cause-and-effect terms as part of the fun
why: UnspeakablePlays' prank tour pauses to rebuild trap mechanisms (a gate under fake water, a delayed timer) while his creature video never does; Jesse Gillett's forensics sit at the far pole. For a tech-curious audience this is the difference between spectacle and a lesson hiding inside spectacle.
evidence_needed: Post-surprise segments from at least three creators; classify each as reconstruction, verdict-only, or move-on.

question: When someone else produces the best moment - a friend lands the line, a builder makes the trap, an artist makes the piece - how much does the creator amplify and credit them versus absorbing the moment into their own narration?
pole_low: absorbs: others' moments become the host's material without credit
pole_high: crowns: repeats, celebrates and credits the actual maker on camera
why: UnspeakablePlays crowns his trap-builders and repeats friends' lines; MoreAliA stops to appreciate original artists and their hours. Credit direction shapes whether an avatar feels generous or extractive - and it models behaviour for the kid coaching it.
evidence_needed: Segments where a non-host produces the peak moment, from at least three creators; code the host's next thirty seconds for credit, repetition or absorption.

question: How much does the creator's self-disclosure cost them - admissions that are genuinely unflattering or status-lowering - versus staying in safe, flattering relatability?
pole_low: disclosure is safe: charming foibles only, nothing that lowers status
pole_high: disclosure costs: real deficits and embarrassments admitted plainly
why: MoreAliA admits a hearing processing lag and declining maths inside a light reaction video; that candour is a trust signal a scripted persona rarely risks. It decides how honest Our Guy can be about its own limits, next to the no-effect honesty questions in the nudge cluster.
evidence_needed: Self-disclosure segments from at least three creators, coded for whether the admission would lower a stranger's estimate of them.

question: Do the creator's callbacks point mostly to shared cultural memory (school, childhood, memes anyone lived) or to proprietary channel memory (own rituals, own past videos, own running gags)?
pole_low: callbacks are cultural: anyone's nostalgia does the work
pole_high: callbacks are proprietary: the channel's own history does the work
why: MoreAliA uses both in a single channel: his relatable format runs on cultural memory while his subscribe-animation ritual is pure proprietary memory, and UnspeakablePlays leans proprietary (cast, past videos). The mix decides whether a new viewer feels included or initiated - a real design choice for the avatar's memory use.
evidence_needed: Callback segments from at least three creators; classify each callback's referent as cultural or channel-owned.
